names.official: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

summary: The United Kingdom requires an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA, £20, valid 2 years or until the passport expires) from visitors who do not need a visa — including US, EU, Canadian and Australian citizens — while visa nationals apply online for a Standard Visitor visa (£135, stays up to 6 months). British and Irish citizens, and people who already have a UK visa or permission to live, work or study in the UK, do not need an ETA.

defaultStayWindow.text: The allowance runs per visit rather than across a window: the Home Office prices its long-term Standard Visitor visas at “6 months per visit”, and the guide states you can usually stay up to 6 months. GOV.UK says visitors cannot live in the UK for long periods through frequent or successive visits, but no official source we could read states a numeric limit on how much of the year visits may add up to. GOV.UK does not say whether the days of arrival and departure are counted, so we count both.

source.name: GOV.UK — Standard Visitor: apply for a Standard Visitor visa

fee.notes: Apply via the official UK ETA app or GOV.UK. Every traveler needs their own ETA, including babies and children.

items.name: Photo of the passport
items.details: The passport you will travel with. On the app you scan it with your phone's camera.

items.name: Photo of the applicant's face
items.details: Must follow the rules for digital photos of faces, or the application may be delayed or rejected.

source.name: GOV.UK — Get an electronic travel authorisation (ETA) to visit the UK: Apply for an ETA

fee.notes: Apply online, then attend an appointment at a visa application centre. Long-term 2, 5 and 10-year visitor visas cost £506, £903 and £1,128; each still allows 6 months per visit.
Plus the healthcare surcharge, paid as part of the application. Requires a place on a course offered by a licensed student sponsor; decisions usually take 3 weeks from outside the UK.

source.name: GOV.UK — Skilled Worker visa (fees vary by visa length and role — check the current fee on GOV.UK)

fee.notes: For passing through UK border control and leaving the UK within 48 hours; GOV.UK gives the fee as £74.50. A Direct Airside Transit visa covers changing flights without going through border control.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for the whole of your stay in the UK.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel insurance requirement for the UK. GOV.UK says overseas visitors are charged 150% of the cost of NHS treatment unless they are exempt, that people on a visitor visa or a visa of under 6 months pay for healthcare at the point of use unless exempt, and that A&E services are free of charge.

source.name: GOV.UK (Department of Health and Social Care) — NHS entitlements: migrant health guide

onwardTicket.text: GOV.UK says visitors must be able to show that they will leave the UK at the end of their visit and that they can pay for their return or onward journey, or have someone else fund it.

proofOfFunds.text: GOV.UK says visitors must be able to show that they can support themselves and their dependants during the trip, or have funding from someone else; it states no amount.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of £10,000 or more must be declared when carried between Great Britain and a country outside the UK. For Northern Ireland, cash of €10,000 or more must be declared when carried between Northern Ireland and a non-EU country.

source.name: GOV.UK — Taking cash in and out of Great Britain

notes: GOV.UK lists the personal allowance for arrivals in Great Britain as 200 cigarettes (or 250 g of tobacco), 42 litres of beer or cider and 18 litres of wine, plus 4 litres of spirits over 22% ABV (or 9 litres of drinks up to 22%), and other goods worth up to £390.

GOV.UK says you cannot bring meat or meat products, or milk-based products (except powdered infant milk, infant food or special food needed for medical reasons), into Great Britain from countries outside the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, the Faroe Islands and Greenland.

payments.text: Australia's Smartraveller says ATMs are available, credit cards are widely used and contactless payment is widely accepted.

safety.text: Canada advises a high degree of caution in the UK because of the threat of terrorism, and says petty crime such as pickpocketing and purse snatching is common and cellphone theft is common in certain tourist areas of London.

tips.text: GOV.UK says the ETA costs £20 to apply online or through the UK ETA app, that other websites may charge more, and that you cannot get a faster decision by applying through another website or app.
Every traveler needs their own ETA, including babies and children; it is valid 2 years (or until your passport expires) for unlimited visits.

GOV.UK says EU, EEA and Swiss citizens need a valid passport to enter the UK; a national identity card can be used only in some cases, such as by people with settled or pre-settled status or a pending EU Settlement Scheme application, an EU Settlement Scheme family permit, a frontier worker permit, or S2 Healthcare Visitors.
GOV.UK says overseas visitors are charged 150% of the cost of NHS hospital treatment unless they are exempt; A&E treatment is free.

faq.question: What is the UK ETA and who needs it?
faq.answer: The Electronic Travel Authorisation lets visitors who do not need a visa travel to the UK for up to 6 months; GOV.UK says you usually need one rather than a visa if you are from Europe, the USA, Australia, Canada or certain other countries. It costs £20, lasts 2 years or until your passport expires, whichever is sooner, and allows as many visits as you want. British and Irish citizens, UK visa holders and people with permission to live, work or study in the UK do not need one.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for the UK?
faq.answer: No visa, but they do need an ETA: US passport holders must obtain the £20 Electronic Travel Authorisation before traveling and can then visit for up to 6 months per trip.

faq.question: How much does a UK Standard Visitor visa cost?
faq.answer: The Standard Visitor visa costs £135 for a 6-month visa. Long-term 2, 5 and 10-year versions cost £506, £903 and £1,128, and each allows 6 months per visit.

faq.question: Can EU citizens enter the UK with a national ID card?
faq.answer: Usually not. GOV.UK says EU, EEA and Swiss citizens need a valid passport, and accepts a national identity card only in some cases, such as from people with settled or pre-settled status or a pending EU Settlement Scheme application, an EU Settlement Scheme family permit, a frontier worker permit, or S2 Healthcare Visitors. Visitors who do not need a visa also need a £20 ETA; Irish citizens do not.

faq.question: How long can visitors stay in the UK?
faq.answer: Visitors with an ETA, and Standard Visitor visa holders, can usually stay up to 6 months per visit. GOV.UK says visitors cannot do paid or unpaid work for a UK company or as a self-employed person (unless it is a permitted paid engagement or event) or live in the UK for long periods through frequent or successive visits.
